newsitem.title: USA: US jobless rate below 5.5% may up inflation -- Parry.
newsitem.headline: US jobless rate below 5.5% may up inflation -- Parry.

text.p: An unemployment rate below 5.5 percent could, if kept for a long period of time, spark inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy, Robert Parry President of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco said.

"I suggest that something around 5.5 percent would be the number that one should look at, and if it were to be less than that for a prolonged period of time, you have to become a bit concerned," Parry said when asked about what level of unemployment could trigger inflation. Parry made his remarks during an interview with Nightly Business Report, a public television news program.
Parry said he was somewhat optimistic that U.S. economic growth would slow down in the second quarter from the 5.6 percent expansion rate seen in the first three months of this year.
The San Francisco Fed chief added that he expected second quarter gross domestic product to show a much smaller rate of growth.

"It seems to me highly unlikely that (the first quarter growth rate) is going to continue, and I would expect a fairly significant slowing in the second quarter, although I would find it impossible to give you a number at this point," Parry said.
Parry said that the level of the U.S. dollar exchange rate should not be a goal for Federal Reserve monetary policy.
"The value of the dollar is very important in analyzing the economy and what is going to happen to it. But in my mind it should not be a goal or objective of monetary policy."
The head of the San Francisco Fed said a balanced budget agreement reached by the White House and the Republican Congress last week will be helpful.
But he expressed some dissappointment with regard to how the accord addresses entitlement programs.
"It's good to have the accord and it certainly will be helpful, I am a little dissappointed that maybe we are not going to address right away some of the entitlement issues," Parry said.
"I certainly had hoped that maybe we would have a serious attempt to try to deal with the CPI overstatement which I think is part of the problem as well."
